thread:
Ellen: Morning pulse for the release train — short incident during canary traffic shaping for v3.8. Heads-up: temporary freeze likely.
Tom: Canary went live 05:30 UTC. At ~05:38 we saw an uptick in 429s on embeddings-write (p90 up) after we flipped the new throttling policy.
Ravi: Looking at proxy logs: client-side retries amplified when the throttle returned 429s, causing cascading backpressure to workers. Reverting throttle policy on canary now.
Ravi: Command I ran:
```
kubectl -n canary set env deployment/edge-proxy THROTTLE_MODE=legacy
```
deploy-bot: [05:41 UTC] Env change applied to canary edge-proxy. pods: 3/3 ready. (CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/build/1999)
QA-Maya: After revert 429s dropped to baseline in ~2m. QA run shows no data loss. See quick dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/emb/write/errors (watch eu-west)
Ellen: Because this caused user-visible throttling, instituting a short release freeze for config/routing changes 06:00-08:00 UTC. If you need an exemption include impact statement + test plan in this thread.
Tom: Action items: (1) add client-side retry jitter in SDK to avoid synchronized retries, (2) add guardrail to throttle logic to return 503 with Retry-After when queue depth is high, (3) run a staged replay with warmed caches.
Ravi: I'll open follow-ups: infra issue with repro steps and a patch PR for throttle guardrail. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/infra/throttle-guard/334
Ellen: Changelog entry queued: "throttle policy revert on canary; temporary config freeze 06:00-08:00 UTC; follow-up guardrail PR." PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/eng/release-notes/1023
QA-Maya: Kicking off a 30m regression sweep across embeddings read/write surfaces; will post results here.
Ellen: Thanks team — keep updates concise in this thread and tag @oncall if you see customer impact. :white_check_mark:
